claims.text: Surgery can be curative for selected patients with resectable NSCLC, and treatment depends on disease stage, histology and the patient's health.
claims.locator: General Information; Treatment of Stages IA and IB NSCLC

claims.text: The four selected reports do not establish that itraconazole or metformin can replace potentially curative surgery. The presurgical itraconazole study retained planned surgery; the other trials evaluated additional drugs in different treatment settings.
claims.locator: Institutional record Abstract at https://utsouthwestern.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/concentration-dependent-early-antivascular-and-antitumor-effects-/ | Methods: Study Design and Efficacy; Results: Patient Characteristics, Safety and Tolerability, Efficacy; Discussion paragraph beginning There are important caveats | Abstract: Design, Interventions, Main outcomes, Results, Conclusions | Methods: Patient Population, Assessments and Outcomes; Results: Patient Population, Efficacy, Toxic Effects; Discussion and Limitations

claims.text: Gerber and colleagues enrolled 13 patients with NSCLC scheduled for resection. They received itraconazole for 10-14 days before surgery, with imaging, blood and tissue measurements to investigate biological effects.

Higher drug concentrations were associated with greater reductions in tumor volume and perfusion, among other measurements. These short-term associations do not establish improved survival or show that surgery can safely be omitted.

Rudin and colleagues conducted an open-label randomized phase 2 trial in previously treated metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC. It enrolled 23 patients: 15 received pemetrexed plus itraconazole and 8 received pemetrexed alone. The trial closed early because of slow recruitment as pemetrexed use changed.
claims.locator: Methods: Study Design and Efficacy; Results: Patient Characteristics, Safety and Tolerability, Efficacy; Discussion paragraph beginning There are important caveats

claims.text: At 3 months, 67% versus 29% were progression-free (P = .11), the primary endpoint. Median overall survival, an additional endpoint, was 32 versus 8 months (P = .012), favoring the combination. The authors emphasized that the small sample made effect estimates highly unstable.
claims.locator: Methods: Study Design and Efficacy; Results: Patient Characteristics, Safety and Tolerability, Efficacy; Discussion paragraph beginning There are important caveats

claims.text: Reported events in the combination group included transient grade 4 neutropenia without fever and a possibly treatment-related intratumoral bleed within 30 days after leaving the study. This small study cannot establish broad safety or a reliable survival benefit, and it did not study initial treatment of resectable disease.
claims.locator: Methods: Study Design and Efficacy; Results: Patient Characteristics, Safety and Tolerability, Efficacy; Discussion paragraph beginning There are important caveats

claims.text: The U.S. capsule label warns about heart failure, serious liver toxicity and consequential drug interactions, including contraindicated combinations involving CYP3A4 substrates.
claims.locator: Boxed Warning: Congestive Heart Failure, Cardiac Effects and Drug Interactions; Warnings: Hepatic Effects and Cardiac Disease

claims.text: This open-label phase 2 trial studied patients without diabetes who had unresectable stage III NSCLC. Of 170 enrolled patients, 167 eligible patients were analyzed: 86 in the metformin group and 81 in the control group. Both groups received chemoradiation and consolidation chemotherapy.
claims.locator: Abstract: Design, Interventions, Main outcomes, Results, Conclusions

claims.text: The primary endpoint, 1-year progression-free survival, was 51.3% with metformin and 60.4% without it (hazard ratio 1.15; 95% CI 0.77-1.73; P = .24). One-year overall survival was similar, and no significant difference in adverse events was reported. The trial did not demonstrate improved survival with metformin.
claims.locator: Abstract: Design, Interventions, Main outcomes, Results, Conclusions

claims.text: This open-label phase 2 trial randomized 54 patients without diabetes and with unresected stage III NSCLC: 26 to chemoradiotherapy plus metformin and 28 to chemoradiotherapy alone. Recruitment stopped early.
claims.locator: Methods: Patient Population, Assessments and Outcomes; Results: Patient Population, Efficacy, Toxic Effects; Discussion and Limitations

claims.text: The primary composite treatment-failure endpoint occurred within 1 year in 18/26 patients (69.2%) with metformin versus 12/28 (42.9%) in the control group (P = .05). It included progression, death, or stopping trial treatment or planned evaluations for any reason.
claims.locator: Methods: Patient Population, Assessments and Outcomes; Results: Patient Population, Efficacy, Toxic Effects; Discussion and Limitations

claims.text: One-year overall survival was 47.4% versus 85.2% (hazard ratio 3.80; 95% CI 1.49-9.73). At least one grade 3 or higher adverse event was reported in 14/26 (53.8%) versus 7/28 (25.0%), respectively. These are all-cause adverse events, not all established as caused by metformin.
claims.locator: Methods: Patient Population, Assessments and Outcomes; Results: Patient Population, Efficacy, Toxic Effects; Discussion and Limitations

claims.text: The small sample, open-label design and treatment imbalances limit interpretation; the unfavorable findings argue against an anticancer add-on in this setting.
